feedback: Iteration 3 is the key evidence here. Its controller was identical to iteration 1 (base_speed 1.3, kp 2.5, kd 0.3), so you can attribute the drop from 69.32 to 59.64 to the offset change alone, not to a controller change as your rationale suggests. Iteration 2 also held the controller fixed, and its 16 mm footprint fell to 54.45, so 12 mm should stay. Line loss has stayed near 1 per run in every iteration (0 to 3), so the sensor span and footprint have only partly reduced it. Steering oscillation has stayed between 0.09 and 0.15, so it is not the limiting factor. The Integrator's package this iteration restores y=0.05 m with the iteration 1 controller, so the race should show whether the offset was the cause. Do not treat that as a result for this design. For the next geometry, hold y=0.05 m and test a single change: span ±0.04 m. Iteration 0 to 1 raised the score by 15 points by widening the span from ±0.024 to ±0.03 m, though that change was paired with a controller change, so the span effect is only partly isolated. If line loss still persists after the span test, the remaining levers are the forward offset (not y=0.03 m, which iteration 3 ruled out) and the controller, so the Integrator will look at line-loss handling. Keep wheel track, wheel radius, mass and body fixed. Body width does not move the off-track limit, which is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) = 0.06 m across the allowed range.
requested_changes: Hold sensor_size at 0.012 m and the forward offset at y=0.05 m, since iteration 3 (y=0.03 m, same controller as iteration 1) lost about 10 points and iteration 2 (16 mm footprint) lost about 15.
Test a wider span of about ±0.04 m (sensor x at -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04 m) at y=0.05 m as a single geometry change, to see whether the line-loss rate falls further beyond the ±0.03 m span.
If the span test does not reduce line_loss_events below about 1 per run, return to the ±0.03 m span and hold the geometry; do not move the offset again without a controller explanation.
